title: Why Humans Believe in Stories: From Gods to Money and Nations
description:
Why do humans believe in gods, myths, and fairy tales? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we explore how storytelling shaped religion, culture, and conflict.

Drawing from Jonathan Gottschall’s The Storytelling Animal and Yuval Noah Harari’s Sapiens & Homo Deus, we examine how the Cognitive Revolution, Agricultural Revolution, and Scientific Revolution gave humans the unique ability to imagine, cooperate, and build fictional realities. From money and nations to religions and gods, stories became the glue that bound societies together.

But when these stories harden into dogmas, they divide us. From the partition of India and Pakistan to the Israel–Palestine conflict, people kill and die for ancient stories, while taxpayers fund armies to guard imaginary lines. These myths once helped us survive, but today they often fuel wars, terror, and hatred.

👉 If you’ve searched for why humans believe in gods, Yuval Harari storytelling, Sapiens explained, Cognitive Revolution, myths and religion, human cooperation through stories, religion as fiction, God man-made story — this video uncovers how storytelling created both our greatest strengths and our deepest conflicts.

Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share — hype this video so it reaches more people and sparks better conversations!

#ReligionExplained #YuvalHarari #Storytelling #PaleBlueThoughts
